name: HAL Tejas Mk1A

specs.Armament: 23 mm GSh-23 cannon; Astra, R-73, Derby BVR/WVR missiles; precision bombs

desc: India's indigenous 4.5-generation light fighter, the Mk1A adds AESA radar, electronic warfare suite, air-to-air refuelling and BVR missiles. 83 aircraft ordered in 2021 with a follow-on order for 97 more, making it the numerical backbone of the IAF's future fleet.

name: Dassault Rafale (IAF & Navy Rafale-M)
status: In service (36 IAF) / on order (26 Rafale-M)

specs.Engine: 2 × Snecma M88-2 (75 kN each with A/B)
specs.Armament: 30 mm GIAT cannon; Meteor, MICA, SCALP, HAMMER; ~9,500 kg payload

desc: Inducted in 2020 at Ambala and Hasimara, the Rafale brought Meteor beyond-visual-range missiles and SCALP cruise missiles to the IAF. The Navy's 26 Rafale-M will operate from INS Vikrant and INS Vikramaditya.

name: Sukhoi Su-30MKI

specs.Armament: 30 mm GSh-30-1; BrahMos-A, Astra, R-77, R-73; ~8,000 kg payload
specs.Radar: N011M Bars PESA (Virupaksha AESA in Super-30 upgrade)

desc: The IAF's largest fighter fleet and the only aircraft in the world to carry the air-launched BrahMos. The 'Super Sukhoi' upgrade programme will add an indigenous AESA radar, new mission computer and EW suite to 84 aircraft.

name: Dassault Mirage 2000 (I/TI upgrade)

specs.Armament: 2 × 30 mm DEFA; MICA, SCALP, Spice-2000 precision bombs

desc: Star of Kargil (1999) and the Balakot strike (2019), the Mirage 2000 fleet was upgraded to the I/TI standard with new radar, MICA missiles and glass cockpits, extending service into the 2030s.

name: MiG-29K

specs.Armament: 30 mm cannon; R-77, R-73, Kh-35 anti-ship, Kh-31

desc: India's only operational carrier fighter, flying from INS Vikramaditya and INS Vikrant until the Rafale-M and the indigenous TEDBF arrive.

name: AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft)
status: Development — prototype rollout targeted ~2028, induction mid-2030s

specs.Features: Stealth shaping, internal carriage, supercruise (Mk2), sensor fusion

desc: Approved by the Cabinet Committee on Security in 2024 with an execution model open to private industry, AMCA is India's ticket into the stealth club alongside the US, China and Russia.

name: HAL Prachand (Light Combat Helicopter)

specs.Armament: 20 mm turret gun; 70 mm rockets; Mistral AAM; Helina/Dhruvastra ATGM

desc: Designed for Siachen and Ladakh altitudes after Kargil, Prachand can take off and land at 5,000 m with weapons. The March 2025 order of 156 helicopters (₹62,700 crore) is HAL's largest ever.

name: Boeing AH-64E Apache Guardian

specs.Armament: 30 mm M230 chain gun; AGM-114 Hellfire; Stinger; Hydra 70 rockets

desc: The IAF received 22 Apaches from 2019; the Army's six were delivered from 2025 for the Jodhpur-based squadron facing the western front.

name: HAL Dhruv (ALH) & Rudra
desc: The workhorse of Indian military aviation, the Advanced Light Helicopter flies in utility, armed (Rudra), naval and coast guard variants and is exported to Mauritius, Nepal, Maldives and Ecuador.

name: Boeing C-17 Globemaster III
desc: India operates the world's second-largest C-17 fleet, decisive in Ladakh deployments (2020), Operation Ganga (Ukraine) and disaster relief across the Indian Ocean.

name: Lockheed Martin C-130J Super Hercules
desc: Famous for landing at Daulat Beg Oldie (5,065 m) — the world's highest airstrip — the C-130J is the IAF's special-forces transport and Himalayan lifeline.

name: DRDO Netra AEW&C
service: Indian Air Force (3 + 6 Mk1A on order)
desc: Netra directed the 2019 Balakot package and remains India's only indigenous airborne early warning platform; six Mk1A on Embraer airframes and a larger A321-based Netra Mk2 are under way.

name: Arjun Mk1A Main Battle Tank

specs.Upgrades: 72 improvements over Mk1 incl. hunter-killer, remote weapon station

desc: India's indigenous MBT, heaviest in the region, optimised for the Rajasthan desert sector; the Mk1A's 118-tank order (₹7,523 crore) keeps HVF Avadi busy into 2027.

name: T-90S/SK Bhishma
desc: The Army's mainstay MBT since 2003 with over 1,200 in service, licence-produced at Avadi; the Bhishma fleet is being upgraded with new sights, APS trials and the 'Mk III' standard.

name: T-72M1 Ajeya
status: In service (being replaced by FRCV from 2030s)
desc: The most numerous tank in the Indian Army; a 1,000 hp engine upgrade and thermal sights extend life while the Future Ready Combat Vehicle programme takes shape.

name: K9 Vajra-T Self-Propelled Howitzer
desc: Built by L&T at Hazira with over 50% indigenous content, the Vajra was rushed to Ladakh in 2020 with winterisation kits — proof that a desert gun could hold the Himalayas.

name: Dhanush 155 mm Towed Howitzer

specs.Features: Auto gun-laying, inertial navigation, muzzle velocity radar

desc: The 'desi Bofors' — an indigenised, longer-barrel evolution of the FH-77B, with over 80% Indian content and the first of 114 delivered in 2019.

name: ATAGS (Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System)
origin: India (DRDO ARDE with Bharat Forge & TASL)
desc: The ₹6,900 crore order for 307 ATAGS and 327 gun-towing vehicles in March 2025 marked the first major indigenous artillery contract split between two private firms.

name: Pinaka Multi-Barrel Rocket Launcher
desc: Battle-tested in Kargil, Pinaka is now India's first major artillery export (Armenia) with 120 km and 300 km range variants under development.

name: BrahMos Supersonic Cruise Missile
type: Supersonic cruise missile (land, ship, sub, air)
desc: The fastest operational cruise missile in the world and India's first major weapons export (US$375 million Philippines deal, 2022). The BrahMos-NG will fit the Tejas and MiG-29.

name: Agni-V ICBM (with MIRV — Mission Divyastra)
desc: India's longest-range nuclear-capable missile; Mission Divyastra (2024) demonstrated multiple independently targetable re-entry vehicles, a capability held by only a handful of nations.

name: K-4 Submarine-Launched Ballistic Missile
service: Strategic Forces Command / Navy (INS Arihant, Arighaat)
desc: Fired from INS Arighaat in November 2024, the K-4 gives India's sea-based nuclear deterrent genuine second-strike reach — the third leg of the triad.

name: Akash / Akash-NG SAM
desc: The centrepiece of India's layered air defence with S-400 and Barak-8; Akash showed a four-target simultaneous engagement in 2024 and won its first export order from Armenia.

name: S-400 Triumf (Sudarshan Chakra)
desc: The US$5.4 billion S-400 deal reshaped the northern and western air-defence picture; squadrons cover Punjab, Sikkim and the Rajasthan sector.

name: Barak-8 MR-SAM / LR-SAM
desc: Jointly developed and produced with Israel, Barak-8 arms the Navy's Kolkata and Visakhapatnam-class destroyers and the IAF's and Army's MR-SAM regiments.

name: INS Vikrant (IAC-1)
desc: India's first indigenously built carrier and one of the largest warships ever built in the country, with 76% indigenous content by value. A second indigenous carrier (IAC-2) is under consideration.

name: INS Vikramaditya
desc: Commissioned in 2013 after a US$2.35 billion refit at Sevmash, Vikramaditya is the Western Fleet's flagship carrier.

name: Visakhapatnam-class Destroyer (Project 15B)

specs.Armament: 16 × BrahMos, 32 × Barak-8, 76 mm gun, torpedoes, RBU-6000

desc: The most powerful surface combatants built in India — Visakhapatnam, Mormugao, Imphal and Surat — with 75% indigenous content.

name: Nilgiri-class Frigate (Project 17A)
desc: Seven stealth frigates split between Mazagon Dock and Garden Reach — the largest single indigenous warship programme by number of hulls.

name: Kalvari-class Submarine (Scorpène / Project 75)
desc: Kalvari to Vagsheer — six Scorpène boats built at Mazagon Dock; three additional boats and indigenous air-independent propulsion are the next phase.

name: INS Arihant / Arighaat (SSBN)
desc: India joined the six-nation SSBN club with Arihant in 2016; Arighaat (2024) and the larger Aridhaman complete continuous at-sea deterrence.

name: MQ-9B SkyGuardian / SeaGuardian
desc: The US$3.5 billion deal for 31 MQ-9Bs — the Navy already leases two SeaGuardians — gives India persistent ISR over the Indian Ocean and the LAC.

name: IAI Heron Mk II
status: In service (with weaponisation via Project Cheetah)
desc: Fast-tracked under emergency procurement after the 2020 Ladakh stand-off, the Heron Mk II fleet watches the LAC around the clock.

name: DRDO TAPAS-BH 201 (Rustom-II)
desc: India's indigenous MALE drone fell short of the Army's 30,000 ft / 24 h requirement but a reduced batch is being inducted while an upgraded variant is developed with private partners.
